scripts.comment: Providing an input to change the number of branches at each level is harder than we expect students to try; it would involve a FOR loop to vary the number of recursive calls, plus rules to determine the angle and scale factor for each branch.

7.1.5.1: For each of the suggested variations, students might just change the values to new constant values, or they might make the variation user-controllable by changing the values to inputs. Both possibilities are shown below. The problem statement doesn't say that the four suggested variations have to be done separately; it's fine if students do all of them in one procedure. But these solutions do each change separately, so you can see what part of the code changes for each of them.

scripts.comment: 7.1.5.3: Changing the thickness was misleadingly easy; students' analysis of TREE WITH THICK TRUNK may not be entirely right. Trying to color the leaves differently from other branches shows that on its way back down to the trunk, the sprite redraws everything in green. This can be fixed either by moving down with the pen up or by changing the color back to brown after drawing a leaf. The solution below shows both ways.

tree varying branching plus gravity, %br level: %n size: %n gravity strength: %n

scripts.comment: In TREE WITH GRAVITY, instead of figuring out how to undo the effect of gravity to return the sprite to its starting state (position and direction), the program remembers the sprite's starting direction and uses POINT IN DIRECTION to restore that direction regardless of where drawing the subtree left it. (GRAVITY affects only the direction, not the position. If we made some other change that affected the position, we could remember and restore position in the same way.)
